intent: A biodiversity quiz that beats the obvious answer: the word BRAZIL erased when the rainforest giant only comes third, three tallies to scale with the winner on top, the three Andean ranges as the reason, and a pin on the coastal massif where birds exist nowhere else — mountains, not jungle.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which country has the MOST bird species?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which country has the most bird species?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: Colombia. Nearly 2,000 bird species, about a fifth of every bird species on Earth.

lines.direction: ease back over the north of South America; the word BRAZIL stands on 'Brazil' and is erased on 'third'; the Brazilian flag-ball thinks on 'third'; an island sticker on 'fourth' as Colombia pulses
lines.text: Brazil has the Amazon, yet only comes third. Indonesia's many islands come fourth.

lines.direction: tighten on the Andes; three tallies rise to scale on 'Peru' with Colombia on top; the Andes tag plates on 'valley' with a mountain sticker; a wave sticker on 'oceans' as Colombia pulses
lines.text: Peru sits just behind. The secret is 3 Andean ranges, every valley between them breeding its own birds, and coasts on 2 oceans.

lines.direction: drift north to the Caribbean massif; the 160+ card on 'hummingbird' with a feather sticker; the Santa Marta pin on 'anywhere'; a magnifier sticker on 'hills' as the Colombian flag-ball grins and Colombia pulses; the pin leaves at the end
lines.text: More kinds of hummingbird live here than anywhere else, and new species are still being described from these hills.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: A fifth of all birds. Follow us.
